# Implementation Cycles (cycle cards)

This file is CYCLE CARDS, not a task list. Each card is a coherent bundle of named test cases
(the card's content); the builder decomposes each card into concrete tasks at build time, with
the code in view — the decomposition is disclosed in the cycle report, never pre-written here.
Cite spec/design content by ID (US-#, FR-#, SC-#, C-#) — never re-quote it; each test case cites
the ID(s) it covers, each written joined behind its owner per the IDs section of `templates/artifact-format.md` — a US,
FR or SC behind its spec's slug (`` `<spec-slug>` FR-012-<slug> ``), a C- ID behind its product
file's owner: `` `product` `` for the product baseline, the spec's slug for a spec's own file
(`` `product` C-003-<slug> ``). Structure and slicing judgment come from
mochiko:patterns-vertical-tdd (the cycle-card shape). The card's checkbox is the progress surface,
flipped when the cycle's named cases show green against real infrastructure.

## Header

Title "# Implementation Cycles: [FEAT-XXX-<slug> — FEATURE NAME]" plus two generated-from
pointers: (1) the spec folder and the design inputs the cards were authored from —
spec.md, features/FEAT-XXX/sufficiency-report.md, and, where the design phase ran, the
run's architecture.md drawing and its marked entries in the product baselines, read in the
pinned-base diff of .mochiko/product/ (on a zero-gap verdict no design phase ran, so the cards are
authored from spec.md, the report, and the product baselines); (2) Structure:
mochiko:patterns-vertical-tdd (cycle-card shape, slicing judgment).

## Overview

Metric table (Metric | Value): Cycles = [N]; Stories covered = [US-# list — every P1/P2
story on at least one card]. There is no foundation/feature split in the count.

## Cycle Format

Each card is one vertical increment: a coherent bundle of named test cases (expected behaviour,
in the `**TEST:**` grammar — see patterns-vertical-tdd/references/TEST-GRAMMAR.md for the
canonical Setup/Action/Assert/Capture grammar) that demonstrate together. The builder
implements the card test-first (red/green/refactor per mochiko:executing-tdd-cycle,
decomposition at build time), and the cycle is done when its named cases show green against
real infrastructure. The card's checkbox is the progress surface, flipped when the bundle's
cases pass. Where the work opens a new end-to-end path (greenfield / new path), the first
cycle is a walking skeleton; growth on an already-standing path skips it. There is no
foundation/feature card type — `[P]` parallel eligibility derives from a card's
dependencies, not from a type column. Each named test case cites the spec/design ID(s) it
covers.

## Cycle Cards

Cards are listed directly, not grouped by foundation/feature type. Each card carries:
checkbox + the card's joined cycle ID and title (`### - [ ] C<n>-<slug> — <title>`); Stories
(US-# — why these stories/cases form one demonstrable bundle,
<= 2 lines); Depends on; Case (Simple | Split — why, one line | Merge — why, one line);
Brownfield exposure (none | extends `path` | modifies `path` — cycle-level surfaces only);
and the closing `**TEST:**` bundle — one or more named test cases, each opening with
`**Covers**: <spec/design IDs>` (the acceptance-ID citation lives per-case, never a standalone
Acceptance-criteria field) then Setup/Action/Assert/Capture fields per TEST-GRAMMAR.md.
Where a new end-to-end path opens, the first card is a walking skeleton (thinnest path, one
trivial case green). `[P]` marks parallel-eligible cards, derived from dependencies.

Good example:
SAMPLE (illustration only — replace with actual cycles; DO NOT keep the samples in the generated tasks.md):

### - [ ] C1-walking-skeleton-path — Walking skeleton: [thinnest end-to-end path]
- **Stories:** `<spec-slug>` US-1-<slug> — thinnest end-to-end path through all layers, one trivial case green; establishes the production-shaped stack [<= 2 lines]
- **Depends on:** —
- **Case:** Simple
- **Brownfield exposure:** none

**TEST:** [entity] round-trips through the full stack
- **Covers**: `<spec-slug>` US-1-<slug> / SC-001-<slug>
- **Action**: `curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/[entity] -d '{"name":"Test"}'`
- **Assert**: Response status: 201
- **Assert**: Console contains "[entity]_id"
- **Capture**: console

### - [ ] C2-<slug> — [Feature bundle title] `[P]`
- **Stories:** `<spec-slug>` US-2-<slug> — [why these stories/cases form one demonstrable bundle, <= 2 lines]
- **Depends on:** C1-walking-skeleton-path
- **Case:** [Simple | Split — why | Merge — why]
- **Brownfield exposure:** extends `src/models/[entity].py`

**TEST:** [behavior] works end to end via API
- **Covers**: `<spec-slug>` US-2-<slug> / SC-002-<slug> scenario 1
- **Setup**: Seed prerequisite [entity] data
- **Action**: `curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/[endpoint] -d '{"[field]":"value"}'`
- **Assert**: Response status: 200
- **Assert**: Console contains "[expected field]"
- **Capture**: console

**TEST:** [behavior] rejects [invalid case]
- **Covers**: `<spec-slug>` US-2-<slug> / SC-002-<slug> scenario 2
- **Setup**: Seed prerequisite [entity] data
- **Action**: `curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/[endpoint] -d '{"[field]":"invalid"}'`
- **Assert**: Response status: 400
- **Capture**: console

## Conformance

Checked mechanically before the write lands. Each line is a string or a count, never a judgment.

- Required headings, in order: `## Overview`, `## Cycle Format`, `## Cycle Cards`
- An undeclared `##` heading is denied. `###` and deeper are yours.
- Line budgets, each counted from its `##` line to the next `##`, nested content included:
  - `## Overview` — 8 lines
  - `## Cycle Format` — 6 lines
- Placeholder tokens that must not survive: `[thinnest end-to-end path]`, `[Feature bundle title]` — checked in frontmatter values and heading text, by exact spelling.

## Skeleton

# Implementation Cycles: [FEAT-XXX-<slug> — FEATURE NAME]

> Generated from the spec folder and the design inputs the cards were authored from: spec.md, features/FEAT-XXX/sufficiency-report.md, and, where the design phase ran, the run's architecture.md drawing and its marked entries in the product baselines, read in the pinned-base diff of .mochiko/product/
> Structure: `mochiko:patterns-vertical-tdd` (cycle-card shape, slicing judgment)

## Overview

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Cycles | [N] |
| Stories covered | [US-# list — every P1/P2 story on at least one card] |

## Cycle Format

Each card is one vertical increment: a coherent bundle of **named test cases** (expected behaviour,
in the `**TEST:**` grammar — see [`TEST-GRAMMAR.md`](../skills/patterns-vertical-tdd/references/TEST-GRAMMAR.md)
for the canonical Setup/Action/Assert/Capture grammar) that demonstrate together. The builder
implements the card test-first (red/green/refactor per `mochiko:executing-tdd-cycle`,
decomposition at build time), and the cycle is done when its named cases show green against real
infrastructure. **The card's checkbox is the progress surface**, flipped when the bundle's cases
pass. Where the work opens a new end-to-end path (greenfield / new path), the **first cycle is a
walking skeleton**; growth on an already-standing path skips it. There is no foundation/feature
card type — `[P]` parallel eligibility derives from a card's dependencies, not from a type
column. Each named test case cites the spec/design ID(s) it covers.
